summary: Describes the messages and procedures of the NACK-Oriented Reliable Multicast (NORM) protocol. It provides end-to-end reliable transport of data objects or streams over IP multicast, with receivers asking for repairs by sending negative acknowledgments. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: When a teacher reads to a whole class, students only raise a hand if they missed a part. NORM works like that, so the sender repeats only what some listeners say they missed.

questions: how does nack-oriented reliable multicast work
